tasks.short: Maintain and order telecommunications equipment stock

steps.what: Count stock into item rows
List items that sit under the minimum
Sign the order list for this count
Confirm lead time with the supplier
Create purchase lines from that list
Match a receipt to an open line
Review a receipt that does not match

tasks.design: Equipment stock lives as rows on the {OPS_SYSTEM}: item id, site, quantity, minimum and serial. A {BI} view lists rows under the minimum. The telecommunications specialist signs the order list for that count and confirms lead time with the supplier. The {PROCUREMENT} lines are created only from that signed list. A receipt updates the same item id, and a mismatch stays for a person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts sat in a private workbook and orders were typed again into purchasing, so the two lists drifted.
tasks.enabler_now: Item id can be the same on the stock row and the purchase line, so a short row can raise an order without retyping.
tasks.still_hard: A minimum that is wrong still orders the wrong quantity, and some spares sit with a supplier the system cannot see.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist sets the minimum, signs what to order, and stops a line that looks wrong.

ambition.what: Review shortages every month, not only when a site has already run out

tasks.altitude: Counting and retyping shrink. The specialist can block an order that is not on the signed list. The supplier call stays.

reach.task: Place the order the specialist signed
reach.learn: Which items are short and which order version is current

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm the equipment inventory is often a workbook plus a separate order. The rows can move; the order decision should not.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A stock row stores item, site and quantity, not how a person used the device.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task is stock and the order list for premises equipment, access spares and backbone spares. Paying the invoice is a later task.

Input contract: item id, site, quantity on hand, minimum, serial, order quantity. Producer is the stock count, or the specialist when a delivery note has no item id. Rows with no item id are not ordered.

Use the operations system's own stock fields and the purchasing requisition before custom code. Supplier-held stock that is not visible stays on the manual call. The supplier meeting stays a conversation.
unknowns: Which spares a carrier holds and will not show.
Who may sign an order list when the specialist is away.
research_questions: What share of items has no minimum?
How often does a receipt fail to match an item id?

already_counted.description: Order-list judgement stays with the specialist
Supplier call time stays with the specialist
Mismatch review stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add minimums when a new item type is stocked
Warehouse staff correct serials the match rejects

approvals.approved_version: order list signed for this stock count

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many items are still counted on paper at small sites, so only the order form is new. The high case assumes counts are clean but every order list and every supplier call still happen. Invoice payment is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare system activity and performance reports

steps.what: Refresh the counter extract for the period
Build the activity and performance tables
Draft comments that cite counter rows

loop.input: performance table cells and the comment template
loop.output: comments that cite a circuit id
loop.check: Every figure in a comment equals a table cell
loop.stop: Drop a sentence that has no circuit id, then stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a movement matters is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Sign the report version
File the signed performance report

tasks.design: A scheduled {BI} report reads circuit, device and trunk counters from the {OPS_SYSTEM} for a fixed period. A bounded note in {DOCS} may comment only on those rows. The telecommunications specialist signs the report version. The report does not name a person and does not change the network.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were copied into a document by hand, and a comment could not show which counter it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Counters can be exported with a circuit id and a period, so every figure can be checked against a cell.
tasks.still_hard: Saying whether a busy trunk is a problem for the business is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which movements matter and which are normal for that site.

ambition.what: Publish the same performance report every month, including sites that used to be skipped

tasks.altitude: The table builds itself. The specialist can refuse a comment that cites no counter.

reach.task: Use the signed report when sizing a link
reach.learn: Which periods are signed and which circuits the specialist marked

evidence.claim: Performance reports in a mid-size firm are a counter export plus a short comment. The numbers should come from a query, not from a prompt.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. The report stores circuit and device counters, not message contents.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends at a signed report. Changing capacity is a later task.
Input contract: period, circuit id, device id, counter name, value, site. Producer is the monitoring export. A counter with no circuit id is dropped, not estimated.
Use the dashboard's own scheduled report before custom code. This task is a screen and a document. The small meeting share fits a sign-off, not a workshop.
The report is not staff monitoring. Per-person traffic is out of scope. If that is requested later, works-council consent applies and this design stops.
unknowns: Which devices export counters and which need a manual reading.
Who is on the distribution list for the signed report.
research_questions: What share of circuits had a missing counter last month?
How often does the specialist delete a drafted comment?

already_counted.description: Comment review stays with the specialist
Report sign-off stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Update the report template when a new counter appears

approvals.approved_version: performance report signed for this period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many devices have no export, so the specialist still types those rows. The high case assumes the query is complete but every comment is still reviewed and signed. Capacity changes are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare purchase requisitions for telecom equipment

steps.what: Submit the item, quantity and site
Prepare the requisition lines
Attach the last price for each item
Check the need text against the item

loop.output: a pass or fail flag per line
loop.check: The flag is only pass or fail, and fail means the text does not name the item id
loop.stop: One pass; every fail goes to the specialist and the loop stops
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text needs are not a fixed code, so a lookup cannot judge the sentence

steps.what: Sign the requisition version
Submit the signed requisition
Buyer receives the submitted requisition

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} form takes item id, quantity, site, cost centre and the technical need. Last price is read from {PROCUREMENT}. A bounded check flags a need that does not name the item. The telecommunications specialist signs the requisition version, and only that version is submitted. The buyer may reject it. The specialist does not approve the spend.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requisitions were rebuilt from mail and old documents, so the item id and the price were retyped and often wrong.
tasks.enabler_now: Item id, cost centre and last price can be fields, so a line can be checked before anyone signs.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a supplier or accepting a higher price is a commercial call the specialist does not own.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist confirms the line is the right item for the site and signs that version.

ambition.what: Raise the requisition when the stock list is signed, instead of batching it at month end

tasks.altitude: Less retyping of lines. The specialist can refuse a line with no item id. Spend approval stays with the buyer.

reach.task: Approve or return the signed requisition
reach.learn: Which lines are technically signed and which prices are only last-paid

evidence.claim: Requisitions in a mid-size firm follow a fixed line layout. The technical check is the specialist's part; the spend approval is not.
Last price and item id are already fields in a purchasing system. The remaining work is the technical signature and the lines that arrive without an item id.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when the requisition version is submitted. Supplier selection and payment are later tasks.

Input contract: requisition id, item id, quantity, site, cost centre, need text, last price, requester. Producer is the signed order list or the engineer who needs a tool or a cable. Lines with no item id or no cost centre are rejected by rule.
Use the purchasing system's own requisition before custom code. The low meeting share fits: this is a screen and a document, not a workshop.
unknowns: Whether the buyer requires a second quote above a set amount.
Who may sign the technical line when the specialist is away.
research_questions: What share of lines is returned for a wrong item id?
How often is last price far from the later quote?

already_counted.description: Line preparation review stays with the specialist
Technical signature stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep the item and cost-centre map current
Requesters fix lines the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: requisition version signed for this requisition id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many requests still arrive as mail with no item id, so the specialist retypes them. The high case assumes clean lines but every technical signature still happens. Payment and supplier choice are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Implement security controls for systems and data

steps.what: Read security gaps on operating systems
Draft controls for software and data

loop.input: gap rows and the control template
loop.output: a change note that cites control ids
loop.check: Every setting cites a control id on the gap list
loop.stop: One draft; drop a line with no control id and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: The reason to accept an exception is not a fixed table

steps.what: Sign the control version and the rollback
Comment on the control gap
Apply the signed security controls
Apply an exception on a manual device

tasks.design: Control rows in {DOCS} name the system id, the setting, the owner and the rollback. A {BI} view shows where the live setting on the {OPS_SYSTEM} differs. The telecommunications specialist signs one control version. A standard setting is applied only for that version. Exceptions, and devices with no job interface, are changed by hand against the same version. Nothing is applied unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: The desired setting lived in a mail thread, so a job could not know which version was approved.
tasks.enabler_now: A control id and a system id can be compared with the live setting, so the gap is a row.
tasks.still_hard: Leaving a risky exception open is a business trade-off, and some appliances have no job interface.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist signs the setting and the rollback, and can stop a change that looks wrong.

ambition.what: Review control exceptions every month, not only after an incident

tasks.altitude: Less time collecting screenshots. The specialist keeps the right to refuse a live change.

reach.task: Check the control the specialist marked as applied
reach.learn: Which version is signed and which systems were skipped

evidence.claim: Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service for mid-size firms that uses models to speed investigation, while analysts still decide. Detection is not the same as applying a setting.

Digest [S16] and [S18] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and, for firms in scope, the duty of care includes patching and supply-chain measures. Scope depends on sector and size.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A control log should record the setting and the owner, not the contents of traffic.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so a control is applied only after a signed version, never unattended.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task is applying a signed control on systems this role runs. Statutory incident reports are a later task and are not treated as done here.

Input contract: control id, system id, setting name, desired value, owner, rollback value. Producer is the control catalogue or the information security analyst. A row with no system id is not applied.
Configure the platform's own baseline and change window before custom code. Appliances with no job interface stay manual, which is why the saved range sits below the central case.

The design does not score people and does not record staff behaviour. A control that would do either stops for a separate review. Works-council consent would be required before any staff-monitoring control.
unknowns: Whether this firm is in scope of the Dutch cyber duty of care.
Which systems are frozen outside a change window.
Who signs when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of controls has no owner?
How many systems have no job interface?

already_counted.description: Control sign-off stays with the specialist
Hands-on exception time stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Revise the control catalogue when a new system type is added
Analyst time on extra retests beyond the comment

approvals.approved_version: control version and rollback signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many appliances have no job interface and the catalogue is incomplete, so the specialist still changes them by hand. The high case assumes standard settings apply only after a signature, and every exception still takes specialist time. Incident reports are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist stops retyping stock rows, report tables and requisition lines, and keeps the order call, the signatures and the security change.
reach: Buyers place the order from the signed stock list and the signed requisition, not from a workbook in mail.
Information security analysts can see which control version was signed and which systems were skipped.
skills_to_grow: Keep equipment stock as a counted row with a minimum and an item id.
Bind a performance figure to a counter extract, not to a typed table.
State a security setting as a reversible value with an owner and a rollback.
role.ambitious_version: Stock, the monthly report and the requisition all use the same item id, and no security setting changes without a signed version.
